clue.text: Is girl embraced by boy about to get the sack?

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
about signals that the word for boy is turned round, written back to front

parts.note: a boy is a lad
taken as written
a girl, as a title, is Miss

explanation.surface: A boy wraps an arm round a girl, and is promptly fired for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is MISS, the title for an unmarried woman, not a name; the boy is a lad, and about turns him round to wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack is British slang for being fired, and dismissal is the formal word for that firing.

clue.text: Bit of colour in line of text?

definitions.meaning: a ... of colour is a small touch of it
a short horizontal punctuation stroke in written text

explanation.definitionFit: A dash can be a small splash of something, and it is also the punctuation stroke in writing.

clue.text: Nosy type soon disturbed, person half hidden

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of soon are jumbled up
half hidden means only the first half of the word person shows, the rest is out of sight

explanation.surface: A nosy person is soon unsettled, partly hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges SOON to SNOO; 'half hidden' keeps PER, the front half of PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooper pries into other people's affairs, the very model of a nosy person.

clue.text: Type of dairy product maiden dished out

indicators.note: dished out says the maiden is served away, removed from the word

parts.note: milk is the basic dairy product
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A kind of dairy product being served by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or sort, as in people of that ilk, so it matches type.

clue.text: Fight ending in horrible graze

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the word horrible

explanation.surface: A brawl finishing in a nasty cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a minor abrasion of the skin, the same injury as a graze.

clue.text: Old chemist who could make air so vile

indicators.note: could make says the following letters can be rearranged to form the name

explanation.surface: A chemist of old who could turn the atmosphere foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Lavoisier was an eighteenth-century French scientist, the father of modern chemistry, who named oxygen.

clue.text: Fellow that sits in the Irish Sea

definitions.meaning: a fellow is a male person, a chap

definitions.text: that sits in the Irish Sea
definitions.meaning: the Isle of ... lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between England and Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a male person, and the island in the Irish Sea is the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Artist making endless cash over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the next
endless says the word for cash loses its last letter

parts.note: cash means money

explanation.surface: A painter keeps making cash without end over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the water lilies.

clue.text: Numbers entertaining deranged tramps?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: deranged means mad

explanation.surface: A crowd of people play host to some crazed vagrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads wander without a settled home, so the clue's question mark admits they are loosely tramps.

clue.text: Rude gesture comes with little hesitation in game

parts.note: to cock a snook is to thumb your nose, a rude gesture
er is the small sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone makes a rude gesture and then hesitates a little during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game played on a large table with red and coloured balls.

clue.text: Have no money — malice is concealed

indicators.note: is concealed says the letters needed lie tucked away inside the words Have no money

explanation.surface: Someone broke resents those with cash but keeps the spite out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in its figurative sense is bitter spite, a close synonym of malice.

clue.text: Suitable land finally commandeered

parts.note: suitable means appropriate

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word land

explanation.surface: Fitting land is at last seized by someone in authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer something is to take it for your own use, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Doesn't forget about those who have paid their subs?

parts.note: re means about, concerning

parts.words: those who have paid their subs
parts.note: people who pay subscriptions to a club are its members

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the matter of who has paid their dues.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to keep it in mind, the opposite of forgetting it.

clue.text: Chief, endlessly formal

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for chief loses its final letter

parts.note: chief means prime, foremost

explanation.surface: A chief who is forever stiff and formal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly proper and correct in manner, a near-synonym of formal.

clue.text: I am leading very good group of warriors

indicators.note: leading says the first piece goes in front of the next one

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
pi is slang for pious, very good

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of heading a fine band of fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword convention for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors.

clue.text: In leisure activity I am covered in glue

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: paste is a kind of glue
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: A hobbyist confesses to being smothered in glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby, something done to pass the time pleasantly.

clue.text: Fellow starts to exclaim loudly in place of worship

parts.note: a fellow is a chap

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of exclaim and loudly

explanation.surface: A man begins shouting out in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a nonconformist place of worship.

clue.text: Woman among bravest heroines

indicators.note: among says the letters lie within the run of words bravest heroines

explanation.surface: A woman who counts among the boldest heroines.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a woman's name, also the Old Testament queen, an example of a woman.

clue.text: Principal desires maths to be given new look

indicators.note: giving the letters a new look means rearranging them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A school head wants the mathematics curriculum overhauled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be given new look' rearranges the letters of DESIRES and MATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal can be a noun for the head of a school, which in a girls' school is the woman in charge.

clue.text: Passage offered by old ship not good

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is left out

parts.note: a galley is an old oared ship

explanation.surface: A route offered by an ancient vessel that is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings.

clue.text: N Europeans rejecting loud places to drink in

indicators.note: rejecting says the letter for loud is thrown out

parts.note: Finns are northern Europeans from Finland
F is forte, the musical sign for loud

explanation.surface: Scandinavians shunning noisy bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are pubs, establishments where one can buy and drink alcohol.

clue.text: Garden plant turned up at front of London school

indicators.note: at front of places the first piece ahead of the second
turned says the little word up is flipped round

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A plant sprouts up in front of a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are plants of the pea and bean family, grown in vegetable gardens.

clue.text: Old ruler had managed to seize India's capital

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to seize says one piece grabs another and holds it inside

parts.note: managed means ran, as in ran a business

indicators.note: capital means the opening letter of the word India's

explanation.surface: A former ruler once managed to capture India's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, but it means the first letter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman emperor of the second century, best known for his wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Academic party joined by any number

parts.note: a do is a party
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A university lecturer's celebration gets crowded with guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Sort of line in grassy area

definitions.meaning: a ... line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites
a lea or pasture field put down to grass

explanation.definitionFit: Ley lines are alleged alignments of old landmarks, and a ley is also land temporarily under grass.

clue.text: Runners bringing computer peripheral aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard says one piece is carried inside the other, as cargo on a vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a printer is a device attached to a computer

explanation.surface: Athletes carry a printer on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinters are athletes who race over short distances, so they are runners.
